memo.signal_conflict: Signal conflict: the model score 5.1e-05 (risk band low; evidence score:198741596) and the structural pattern chain (evidence direction raises_risk; evidence typology:198741596) point in different directions.

claims.text: The transaction matched a chain structural pattern with a chain_len of 7, which exceeds the threshold of 4 and was observed in data with a baseline_illicit_rate of 0.115809 and an observed_illicit_rate of 0.257318.
Model health check status is ok with a window_recall of 0.99005, a reference_recall of 0.98308, and 402 illicit transactions in the window.
Features f53 and f59 pushed the score up; features f18, f52, and f132 pushed the score down.

background.paraphrase: FATF guidance discusses virtual asset red flags including cases where multiple layering of fiat funds was arranged prior to virtual asset purchases.
background.quote: In addition, multiple layering of the fiat funds was arranged prior to the VA purchase by mules.

background.paraphrase: FinCEN guidance notes that suspicious activity indicators include an unusually complex series of transactions indicative of layering activity involving multiple accounts, banks, parties, and jurisdictions.
background.quote: • unusually complex series of transactions indicative of layering activity involving multiple accounts, banks, parties, jurisdictions;

limitations: The Elliptic dataset has no wallet addresses, names, amounts or dates, so none of these appear in this memo.
The model's recall collapsed after time step 43 (a dark-market shutdown), and the model-health check only detects such a collapse several steps later, so scores at later time steps may be unreliable.
Regulation retrieval is weak (hybrid hit@3 about 0.6 on a small test set): retrieved passages are leads for an analyst, not verified authorities, and text from the India document comes from OCR.
Scores are raw gradient-boosting outputs, not calibrated probabilities; the calibrated value shifts with the prevalence of illicit activity.
Structural patterns are resemblances only: Elliptic has no typology labels.
The model-health monitor uses labels with a 2-step lag and a 3-step window, so it cannot flag a collapse in its first steps. On this dataset it first flags at step 47.
This is a draft for a human analyst. It does not decide whether a report should be filed.
